steps.text: Adjust the risk controls, pick a mode and practise on the demo before going live.

pros: Funding by card, transfer, PayPal and Skrill.
cons: Registration details not stated up front.
The demo claim buried in the signup flow.
Performance examples without dates or proof.
Asset list that shifts between pages.
redFlags: Return claims without verification.
The fee that is not a fee: spreads embedded in every trade.
Restriction lists that name different countries.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$250 minimum.
10 crypto assets through broker partners, per the published pages. The list varies between sections, so check the dashboard after signup.
Yes - signup is free and activates through a confirmation link. The first cost is the US$250 deposit, which stays in your trading balance.

faqs.q: Where is Slide Evex Neo restricted?
faqs.a: The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.
The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.

bottomLine: The service behind the marketing looks functional, and a careful user can use it without stepping on the fine print.
Our 4.5 reflects what the pages publish and what they skip. It is not a warning off - it is a reminder to trade the product, not the pitch.
